subject: Customer data use: training assurances, retention windows, and deletion flow
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@greenfield.health>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greenfield.health>
Date: 2028-11-19T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Data use question: training & deletion timelines

Hi Ava,

Following up from our demo — Greenfield Health is evaluating Redwood for PII-containing clinical summarization. Before procurement can move forward we need explicit language on two items for our security and legal teams:

1) Training assurances: does Redwood use customer-provided content (API inputs, uploaded files, transcripts) to train or improve Redwood's models? If not, please state the exact contractual wording you can provide.

2) Retention & deletion: what are the retention windows for (a) raw request/response content, (b) operational logs and traces, (c) backups/snapshots, and (d) ephemeral caches (KV cache, in-memory serving state)? If a deletion request is submitted, what is the lifecycle and SLA for removing data from all stores (including backups)?

We need concrete timelines and a short list of exceptions (if any). Also please attach any relevant factsheets or DPA drafts.

Thanks — Simon
Simon Lewis
Head of Procurement
Greenfield Health
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@greenfield.health>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@greenfield.health>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-19T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Data use question: training & deletion timelines

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details below. Attached: redwood-data-handling-factsheet.pdf and a sample DPA (DPA_redwood_v2.docx).

Executive summary (for procurement/legal):
- Training: By default, Redwood does NOT use Customer Content to train, tune, or improve models in Redwood's model catalog. Any use of Customer Content for model training requires an explicit, documented opt-in (written agreement).
- Retention: default operational retention windows (hosted API) are: request/response payloads retained for 30 days; operational logs/traces retained for 90 days; backups and snapshots retained up to 90 days for disaster recovery. Ephemeral serving caches (KV cache, in-memory) are not persisted beyond the request lifecycle except for short-lived cache entries configurable per customer and typically TTL < 24 hours.
- Deletion SLA: when a verified deletion request is submitted via our support portal or contract clause, we remove active copies within 48 hours and purge recoverable backups within 30–90 days depending on the storage tier. We provide a deletion certificate once the workflow completes.

More detail:
1) Training assurances
- Hosted API: Customer Content is isolated per-account. We run telemetry and internal metrics for service health (e.g., latency, error rates); telemetry aggregates and does not include Customer Content for training. Engineering may use synthetic or redacted examples for debugging with customer approval.
- Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer Content remains under customer control; Redwood does not have access to content for training unless explicitly granted.
- Opt-in programs: We occasionally run opt-in data contribution programs for model research; these are strictly opt-in, opt-in is recorded, and contributions are subject to separate terms.

2) Retention breakdown
- Request/response payloads: default 30 days (configurable down to 0 days for Dedicated/Private where data residency requires it).
- Logs & traces: 90 days by default; shorter retention available on request for enterprise contracts.
- Backups/snapshots: up to 90 days to support restore; snapshot lifecycle may be extended for accounts with specific business continuity requirements (we will note that in the DPA/addendum).
- Ephemeral caches: KV caches used to accelerate inference are in-memory and either scoped to a session or stored in ephemeral cache nodes; they are not used for offline training and are cleared on restart.

3) Deletion process and evidence
- Submit: deletion ticket via support portal (SUP-4591) or contract clause triggers case.
- Within 48 hours: active data removed from primary stores and serving clusters.
- Within 30–90 days: data removed from backup/archival tiers in accordance with storage provider retention windows.
- Certificate: we provide a signed deletion certificate and a checklist of stores purged.

Exceptions & notes
- Aggregated telemetry and metrics (no PII) may be retained indefinitely for product analytics; we can provide an export if needed.
- If Customer exports or caches data in their environment (e.g., Dedicated snapshots), Redwood cannot delete those copies; include this limitation in procurement language.
- Legal holds: we will follow any lawful preservation request and will notify the customer of preservation scope/time.

Suggested contract wording you can use verbatim:
"Redwood Inference does not use Customer Content to improve or train Redwood's machine learning models, model weights, or other model artifacts, except where Customer has explicitly opted in via a separate written agreement. Redwood will delete Customer Content from active stores within forty‑eight (48) hours of a verified deletion request and will purge recoverable backups within thirty (30) to ninety (90) days depending on storage tier. Redwood will provide a deletion certificate upon completion of the deletion workflow"

If you want, Ben can add the formal language into the DPA draft. Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call if your security team wants to walk through the flows.

Best,

Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Simon — quick operational note to confirm the deletion flow differences: for Hosted accounts we run the 48h active purge + 30–90d backup purge timeline. For Dedicated customers we can (and do) configure zero-day retention for request logs and shorter backup TTLs at contract signing; Private/on‑prem deployments are under customer control. I added SUP-4591 so our ops team will track the request.

-Ben

Simon

Hi Simon — here's a short statement you can paste into the DPA or SOW: 

"Redwood Inference does not use Customer Content to train or improve the models in Redwood's public or private model catalogs. Any use of Customer Content for model development requires the Customer's explicit, written opt‑in and will be governed by a separate, documented agreement."

Point of contact for audit inquiries: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.ai), Principal Security Engineer. If you need formal attestation (SOC2 addendum or written letter), let us know and we will coordinate via our security team.

I've attached the DPA_redwood_v2.docx with the suggested clause highlighted. Next step: if procurement is comfortable, we can exchange a redline and I'll loop in contracts.

Regards,
Ava
